newsitem.title: PERU: Peru 28-day CDs draw 12.00 pct avg rate at sale.
newsitem.headline: Peru 28-day CDs draw 12.00 pct avg rate at sale.

text.p: The Central Reserve Bank of Peru said Wednesday it accepted bids for 28-day Certificates of Deposit (CDs) worth 30.0 million soles at an effective average annual rate of 12.00 percent during a bank auction.
The CDs have a June 12 starting date.
The accepted bids also had a minimum and maximum rate of 12.00 percent, the bank said.
At the last CD auction Tuesday, 28-day CDs drew an average rate of 12.41 percent. At Wednesday's auction, the bank said it received bids on the CDs totalling 49.3 million soles.
The bank had offered 30.0 million soles worth of CDs.
Wednesday's sale was the bank's third auction in less than a week. Until last Thursday, the bank had not held a CD auction for two months.
Last year the bank regularly held auctions on Tuesdays and Thursdays but has limited its sales in 1997 due to a lack of liquidity in the financial system.
The average effective annual interest rate for the certificates is used as an informal indicator for interest rates in the Peruvian financial system.
